questions.question: Explain the differences between star and ring topologies in terms of data flow and / failure impact.
questions.solution_html:
• and failure impact.
  • Answer: (Figure (2 marks))
  • Data Flow
  • Data is sent from each device to a central hub or switch, which then forwards it to the
  • destination.(star)
  • Data travels in a circular path (ring) from one device to the next in one direction.(ring).
  • Failure Impact
  • If one device fails, the network continues working. But if the hub fails, the entire network
  • stops.(star)
  • Failure of any single device or connection breaks the ring and can stop the whole
  • network.(ring).

questions.question: Differentiate between micro wave and radio wave.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer: ((2.5 marks) for comparison of each factor)
  •  Microwaves are electromagnetic waves which have frequency range between 1
  • GHz to 300 GHz. These can travel along long distances. These are unidirectional
  • in nature which means that they can travel only in straight line. At very high
  • frequency that cannot penetrate into walls.
  •  The radio waves have frequency range from 3 KHz to 1 GHz.These waves are
  • easy to generate and these can travel along long distances.
  •  These waves are omni directional in nature which means that they can travel in all
  • the directions.
  •  They are widely used for the communication between both indoor and outdoor
  • because they have the property that they can penetrate through the walls very
  • easily.

questions.question: Explain the differences between star and ring topologies in terms of data flow and / failure impact.
questions.solution_html:
• and failure impact.
  • Answer: (Figure (2 marks))
  • Data Flow
  • Data is sent from each device to a central hub or switch, which then forwards it to the
  • destination.(star)
  • Data travels in a circular path (ring) from one device to the next in one direction.(ring).
  • Failure Impact
  • If one device fails, the network continues working. But if the hub fails, the entire network
  • stops.(star)
  • Failure of any single device or connection breaks the ring and can stop the whole
  • network.(ring).

questions.question: Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of using named colors (like “red” or “blue”) / versus hexadecimal codes in HTML.
questions.solution_html:
• versus hexadecimal codes in HTML.
  • Answer 1. Named Colors (e.g., “red”, “blue”, “green”)
  • Benefits
  •  Easy to remember and use — simple names make coding faster.
  •  Readable — improves code clarity, especially for beginners.
  •  No need to know exact color values — quick for basic styling.
  • Drawbacks
  •  Limited choices — HTML supports only around 140 named colors.
  •  Not precise — cannot represent specific shades or custom tones.
  •  Less professional — not suitable for detailed or brand-specific design.
questions.final_answer:  Less professional — not suitable for detailed or brand-specific design

questions.question: Explain the operation of modem.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer: A modem (modulator–demodulator) is a device that enables communication
  • between computers over telephone lines or other analog communication systems.
  • Modulation = Digital → Analog
  • Demodulation = Analog → Digital
  • Modem allows long-distance data communication over analog networks.
questions.final_answer: Modem allows long-distance data communication over analog networks
